title: AN/BYG-1 Applications
description: Description SOLICITATION ANNOUNCEMENT: AN/BYG-1 APPLICATIONS The Department of the Navy, Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA), on behalf of the Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Undersea (PAE Undersea) and the Director, Submarine Programs (DSP), is releasing the formal solicitation for the AN/BYG-1 Applications requirement from the Submarine Combat and Weapons Control Program Office (PMS 425). This notice follows the previously published Draft Request for Proposal (RFP) and Industry Day event. The Government has reviewed the feedback received during and after the Industry Day and has revised the requirements accordingly for this final solicitation. SCOPE OF THE REQUIREMENT (GENERAL OVERVIEW) AN/BYG-1 is the U.S. Navy�s Submarine Combat Control System. The AN/BYG-1 provides tools for the analysis of surface, sub-surface, and airborne contacts operating in the vicinity of own-ship and within the mission theater. This analysis supports command and decision-making, payload and attack control functions, determination of ballistic data for legacy torpedoes, and initiation of firing sequence for all payload types in support of submarine mission areas. The scope of this solicitation encompasses the development, testing, integration, delivery, logistics, and full-lifecycle sustainment of compiled AN/BYG-1 software baselines. This includes current, future, and legacy AN/BYG-1 applications as part of a modernized capability delivery framework. Key objectives and technical efforts under this contract include: Deliver AN/BYG-1 capabilities and baselines in alignment with Submarine Tactical Requirements Group priorities Decouple AN/BYG-1 applications from hardware and software dependencies Implement microcontainer/microservices AN/BYG-1 architecture Transform AN/BYG-1 development and test environments by increasing virtualization and establishing a common, shared infrastructure Develop and integrate tactical decision aids that leverage artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies Assist with the design, development, and integration of combat control system elements to support international cooperative agreements and joint programs. ACCESS TO SOLICITATION DOCUMENTS AND CLASSIFIED DATA The AN/BYG-1 Applications solicitation, Statement of Work (SOW), and associated unclassified attachments are designated as Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and will not be posted directly to SAM.gov. These documents will be made available exclusively via the secure Electronic Technical Information Center (E-TIC) portal hosted by the Advanced Interactive Management Technology Center (AIMTC). Additionally, portions of the Government Furnished Information, specifically, the classified software source code provided to support proposal development are classified at the SECRET level and will be transmitted physically. Documents made available during this procurement may contain classified data and/or technical data whose export is restricted by the Arms Export Control Act. Foreign participation shall be limited by applicable legal authorities, regulations, and other security classification requirements as specified in the DD Form 254. Consolidated Access Request Instructions Prospective Offerors must submit a single, consolidated access request email to the Points of Contact listed below to obtain E-TIC portal access and the classified GFI software package. Email Attachments Required: DD Form 254: A completed copy of the DD Form 254. Block 6 must verify that the requesting company possesses a Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) issued SECRET facility clearance (FCL) and SECRET safeguarding capability. CRITICAL SECURITY NOTE FOR AWARD ELIGIBILITY: While a SECRET FCL is sufficient for proposal preparation and GFI access, the Offeror must ultimately possess a fully adjudicated TOP SECRET facility clearance and TOP SECRET safeguarding capability, issued by the U.S. Government, no later than contract award. The Government will not sponsor facility clearance upgrades or personnel clearance upgrades for the purpose of proposal submission or contract award eligibility. DD Form 2345: A current, approved copy of the company�s DD Form 2345 (Military Critical Technical Data Agreement). Executed Terms of Use Agreement (TOUA): A signed copy of the TOUA, executed by the Offeror's Facility Security Officer (FSO) or authorized corporate representative. Email Body Requirements: Subject Line: Format as N00024-26-R-6222 Access Request - [Insert Company Name]. Company Info: Provide the Company Name and active CAGE Code. E-TIC Representative: Provide the full name, official company email address, and phone number of the designated individual who will serve as the E-TIC account holder. Classified Media Request (Yes/No): State explicitly whether your company is requesting delivery of the classified software source code. Classified Mailing Info (Required only if requesting Classified Media): Provide the name and contact information of the company's FSO, along with the verified Classified Mailing Address of your facility as registered in the National Industrial Security System (NISS). If your company is NOT requesting the classified source code, please state "Not Applicable" or "N/A" for these fields. E-TIC Portal Registration (Unclassified/CUI Documents) Once the Government approves the consolidated request, the designated E-TIC representative must complete their account setup on the AIMTC portal. Access requires a DoD Common Access Card (CAC) or an approved DoD External Certification Authority (ECA) Certificate, along with an active Joint Certification Program (JCP) registration number. For New AIMTC Account Requests: Visit https://aimtc.nuwc.navy.mil and complete the AIMTC Account Request Form. For Existing AIMTC Account Holders: Log into https://aimtc.nuwc.navy.mil, click �My Profile�, and update your fields exactly as follows: Name: First name, middle initial, last name. Foreign National: Select "Yes" or "No". Email Address: Official company email only (no Gmail, Yahoo, etc.). Branch or Code: PMS425 Phone Number: Requestor's direct phone number. NUWC Sponsor POC: Eun-Ja O. Rau NUWC Sponsor Code: PMS425 Justification: "Prospective Offeror for the PMS425 AN/BYG-1 Applications" Scroll down, expand �E-TIC (Electronic Technical Information Center)�, select "BYG-1 Applications Solicitation", provide your justification, and click �Send.� For AIMTC account issues, contact AIMTC_Webmaster@us.navy.mil. Please note that you will not be able to access the PMS425 AN/BYG-1 Applications until your account request is approved by the Approval Official and processed. Please allow for processing. If E-TIC access has not been granted within five (5) business days of your initial email package submission, please contact the Points of Contact listed below for status. The proposal due date will not be extended due to late or incomplete access requests. Over the course of the procurement, the Government may provide E-TIC updates or additional materials to the same designated company representative. Transmission of Classified Media (Software Code) Upon successful verification of the Offeror's FCL, safeguarding capabilities, and NISS mailing address provided in the consolidated email request, and formal approval of the Offeror's E-TIC access (including receipt of the executed TOUA and approved DD Form 2345), the Government will package and transmit the classified media in strict accordance with 32 CFR Part 117 (NISPOM). Classified material will be dispatched via USPS Registered Mail (or Government-approved commercial express carrier authorized for Secret transport). A double-envelope system will be utilized. The outer envelope will feature no classification markings. A signed Classified Material Receipt will be enclosed in the inner envelope. The Recipient must execute and return this receipt to the Government within five (5) business days of delivery. PROPOSAL SUBMISSION Proposals in response

title: USACE - Industry Day 2026
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Middle East District, will host an in-person and virtual Industry Day on 22 October 2026. Check-in on the day of the event will begin at 0730. Tentative agenda will include a Contracting and Programs overview along with a focused session on the upcoming Qatar Development of Al Udeid (QDA) program and an upcoming Space Campus project that is anticipated to be awarded via a new delivery method called Integrated Design and Construction (IDaC). There will be an opportunity for breakout sessions and a question & answer (Q&A) session with Contracting, Construction, Engineering, and Programs and Project Management. The location will be the DoubleTree by Hilton, Blue Ridge Shadows, 111 Hospitality Drive, Front Royal, VA 22630. The purpose of Industry Day is for our architect-engineer and general contractor partners to have a glimpse of the current and upcoming program opportunities in the CENTCOM Area of Responsibility (AOR) to allow both USACE and our contractor community to be better prepared for the work ahead. There will be an opportunity to openly discuss any questions, comments, concerns, and best practices contractors have about working in the CENTCOM AOR during the Q&A session. The Middle East District will solicit questions from industry in advance of the event. Please submit any questions by 1600 Eastern Daylight Time, 16 October 2025 to the attention of Jeanette Farrell at Jeanette.M.Farrell@usace.army.mil, with the Subject Line: Industry Day Oct 2026. Questions will be evaluated, and responses provided during the Q&A portion of the event. All attendees are required to register online to provide their company name and attendee names with titles by 19 October 2026. Please register using the following hyperlink: https://events.dod.teams.microsoft.us/event/e963de64-91e6-4c99-9f20-cf582117491c@fc4d76ba-f17c-4c50-b9a7-8f3163d27582?source=copyLinkLegacyShareLinkDialog When entering the meeting via MS Teams, please enter as a guest utilizing the email provided during registration. We are currently not limiting in-person attendance at the event; however, this may change if an overwhelming number of companies intend to send representatives. A questionnaire is included for the submittal with RSVP. There is no cost to attend this event. Presentation slides will be provided prior to the event. For questions regarding this event, please feel free to contact Jeanette Farrell at the email address shown above.

Introduction: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is pleased to announce the release of Solicitation Number 36C79126R0011, the official Request for Proposals (RFP) for the Electro-Therapeutic Modalities for Pain Management (ETMPM) � Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulation (TENS) Procurement Program. The objective of this national procurement program is to establish multiple single-awards of Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP), Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Base contracts and resultant FFP/IDIQ Delivery Order contracts to be awarded on a per-Contract Line Item Number (CLIN) and per-Sub-Line Item Number (SLIN) basis for the procurement of FDA-cleared electro-therapeutic devices and accessories supporting non-opioid pain management for Veterans across all VA Medical Centers and Community-Based Outpatient Clinics. This solicitation recompetition of the expiring legacy TENS contract and expands the legacy TENS procurement program to include Interferential Current Therapy (IFC) devices, Short-Wave Diathermy (SWD) devices (thermal and non-thermal), and portable Neuromodulation systems - for the treatment of headache disorders to be inclusive all unique parent CLIN devices and the device accessories has enumerated at the discrete subordinate SLINs. The device accessories categorized as SLINs include but are not limited to electrodes, lead wires, power chargers, garment-based applicators, and associated other consumables. Each product of the ETMPM-TENS requirement is mapped to unique parent CLIN and a discrete subordinate SLINs with universal Minimum Technical Requirements (MTRs) applicable to all CLINs/SLINs and individual CLIN/SLIN-specific MTRs. title: USACE - Industry Day 2026
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Middle East District, will host an in-person and virtual Industry Day on 22 October 2026. Check-in on the day of the event will begin at 0730. Tentative agenda will include a Contracting and Programs overview and a focused session on the Qatar Development Area Space Campus. There will be an opportunity for breakout sessions and a question & answer (Q&A) session with Contracting, Construction, Engineering, and Programs and Project Management. The location will be the DoubleTree by Hilton, Blue Ridge Shadows, 111 Hospitality Drive, Front Royal, VA 22630. The purpose of Industry Day is for our architect-engineer and general contractor partners to have a glimpse of the current and upcoming program opportunities in the CENTCOM Area of Responsibility (AOR) to allow both USACE and our contractor community to be better prepared for the work ahead. There will be an opportunity to openly discuss any questions, comments, concerns, and best practices contractors have about working in the CENTCOM AOR during the Q&A session. The Middle East District will solicit questions from industry in advance of the event. Please submit any questions by 1600 Eastern Daylight Time, 16 October 2025 to the attention of Jeanette Farrell at Jeanette.M.Farrell@usace.army.mil, with the Subject Line: Industry Day Oct 2026. Questions will be evaluated, and responses provided during the Q&A portion of the event. All attendees are required to register online to provide their company name and attendee names with titles by 19 October 2026. Please register using the following hyperlink: https://events.dod.teams.microsoft.us/event/e963de64-91e6-4c99-9f20-cf582117491c@fc4d76ba-f17c-4c50-b9a7-8f3163d27582?source=copyLinkLegacyShareLinkDialog When entering the meeting via MS Teams, please enter as a guest utilizing the email provided during registration. We are currently not limiting in-person attendance at the event; however, this may change if an overwhelming number of companies intend to send representatives. A questionnaire is included for the submittal with RSVP. There is no cost to attend this event. Presentation slides will be provided prior to the event. For questions regarding this event, please feel free to contact Jeanette Farrell at the email address shown above.

title: Intelligence Exploitation and Targeting Systems (IETS)
description: The purpose of this Amendment 0002 is to update Attachment 5 L-4 RFP Questions and Responses to respond to industry's second set questions and concerns. The Government will not accept additional questions or concerns after the effective date of this posting. The Naval Air Warfare Center Weapons Division at China Lake, CA is soliciting for an Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Multiple Award Contract (MAC) on a full and open competitive basis for the development and fielding of Development and Fielding of Intelligence Exploitation and Targeting Systems (IETS) systems/prototypes related to future systems and the sustainment of deployed systems. This is a follow-on effort to IDIQ contracts N6893621D-0016 through -0018. The sources sought for this procurement was posted under solicitation N6893625R0030. This requirement will focus on the continued delivery and fielding of IETS that are based upon or derived from the Common Geo-Positioning (CGS) package of software and related hardware components deployed in the Distributed Common Ground System Navy (DCGS) family of programs. This solicitation is being solicited through the Solicitation Module of the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) at https://piee.eb.mil. All submissions in response to this solicitation must be received in the PIEE Solicitation Module, according to the guidance in the Request for Proposals (RFP). Contractors must be certified through Defense Logistics Information Services (DLIS) in order to access Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) or Export Controlled Information. Access to CUI is limited, to a single point of contact (POC) per CAGE code, who is listed as the Data Custodian on the DD 2345 and approved by Defense Logistics Agency (DLA). The DD 2345 must be approved prior to requesting access to CUI in SAM.gov.? Contractors are responsible for coordinating with their CAGE code Data Custodian POC to request access to CUI. For additional information, visit the DLA website for the Joint Certification Program: https://www.dla.mil/HQ/LogisticsOperations/Services/JCP/.?

This solicitation recompetition of the expiring legacy TENS contract and expands the legacy TENS procurement program to include Interferential Current Therapy (IFC) devices, Short-Wave Diathermy (SWD) devices (thermal and non-thermal), and portable Neuromodulation systems - for the treatment of headache disorders to be inclusive all unique parent CLIN devices and the device accessories has enumerated at the discrete subordinate SLINs. The device accessories categorized as SLINs include but are not limited to electrodes, lead wires, power chargers, garment-based applicators, and associated other consumables. Each product of the ETMPM-TENS requirement is mapped to unique parent CLIN and a discrete subordinate SLINs with universal Minimum Technical Requirements (MTRs) applicable to all CLINs/SLINs and individual CLIN/SLIN-specific MTRs. Key Dates: RFP Questions Due-In Date: On or before but no later than October 5, 2026, at 3:00 PM CDT, questions received after this deadline may receive a Government response or receipt acknowledgement. Proposal Package and Product Samples Due-In Date: On or before but no later than October 19, 2026, at 3:00 PM CDT. Early proposal package and product samples are encouraged. Anticipated Award: The results of competition ultimately determine when and if award(s) can be made, but the VA intends to finalize award decisions on or before but no later than January 19, 2027, the expiration date of the legacy TENS contract. The VA reserves the right not to make an award or to make award on some CLINs/SLINs but not all the CLINs/SLINs enumerated in the solicitation. The Small Business size standard for NAICS Code 334510 is 1,250 employees. This NAICS code is appropriate as it encompasses the manufacturing of FDA?regulated electromedical therapeutic equipment including TENS, IFC, neuromodulation, and diathermy devices. PSC: 6515 � Medical and Surgical Instruments, Equipment, and Supplies Set-Aside: The Tiered Set-Aside Evaluation Approach used by the VA is not classified as a traditional Small Business set-aside, but rather as a competitive negotiated procurement, conducted via a tiered evaluation process aimed at prioritizing award to successive small business categories. This acquisition will be conducted using the VA Tiered Set?Aside Evaluation Approach pursuant to the authority of 38 U.S.C. 8127, including the statutory priority ordering prescribed in 38 U.S.C. �?8127(h) (a subsection of the Veterans First Contracting Program statute) and the procedures outlined in Veteran Affairs Acquisition Regulation (VAAR) 815.101?370 (Class Deviation). Under this approach, the Government will solicit offers from all tiers of Offerors simultaneously; however, proposal evaluations and award determination will occur sequentially in the prescribed order of priority. The tiers for this procurement are as follows: Tier-1 Service?Disabled Veteran?Owned Small Business (SDVOSB): SDVOSBs shall be evaluated first in accordance with VA�s statutory obligation to prioritize verified SDVOSBs when the VA Rule of Two is met. If no award can be made at Tier-1, then verified VOSB offers will be evaluated next in Tier-2, consistent with the Veterans First hierarchy. Tier-2 Veteran?Owned Small Business (VOSB): If no award can be made at Tier 2, the Government will evaluate offers from all other eligible small business concerns, (e.g., 8(a), HUBZone, and WOSB are considered before considering other small business concerns), in Tier 3 following the tiering procedures established in VAAR 815.101-3 and VAAR 815.101-370 (Class Deviation). Tier-3 Other Small Business Concerns: If no award can be made at Tier-3, the Government will evaluate offers from all Other-Than-Small-Business (OTSB) Concerns (Large Businesses)) in Tier 4 following the tiering procedures established in VAAR 815.101?3 and 815.101?370 (Class Deviation). Tier-4 Other?Than?Small Business (OTSB) Concerns (Large Businesses): If no award can be made under any small business Tier 1 through 3, the Government will evaluate offers from other?than?small businesses or large business concerns in Tier 4. This tiered evaluation methodology is authorized under 38 U.S.C. 8127 and implemented through the VA�s Class Deviation to VAAR 815.101?370, which permits the use of tiered set?aside procedures to minimize procurement delays in situations where market research indicates that award at the SDVOSB or VOSB tiers is uncertain. The objective of this national procurement program is to establish multiple single-awards of Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP), Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Base contracts and resultant FFP/IDIQ Delivery Order contracts to be awarded on a per-Contract Line Item Number (CLIN) and per-Sub-Line Item Number (SLIN) basis for the procurement of FDA-cleared electro-therapeutic devices and accessories supporting non-opioid pain management for Veterans across all VA Medical Centers and Community-Based Outpatient Clinics. description: Description NOTE: On 8 August 2026, Solicitation Amendment 001 was published in the E-TIC portal, including a revised solicitation, a revised Section L, and a Question & Answer set Batch 1. SOLICITATION ANNOUNCEMENT: AN/BYG-1 APPLICATIONS The Department of the Navy, Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA), on behalf of the Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Undersea (PAE Undersea) and the Director, Submarine Programs (DSP), is releasing the formal solicitation for the AN/BYG-1 Applications requirement from the Submarine Combat and Weapons Control Program Office (PMS 425). This notice follows the previously published Draft Request for Proposal (RFP) and Industry Day event. The Government has reviewed the feedback received during and after the Industry Day and has revised the requirements accordingly for this final solicitation. SCOPE OF THE REQUIREMENT (GENERAL OVERVIEW) AN/BYG-1 is the U.S. Navy�s Submarine Combat Control System. The AN/BYG-1 provides tools for the analysis of surface, sub-surface, and airborne contacts operating in the vicinity of own-ship and within the mission theater. This analysis supports command and decision-making, payload and attack control functions, determination of ballistic data for legacy torpedoes, and initiation of firing sequence for all payload types in support of submarine mission areas. The scope of this solicitation encompasses the development, testing, integration, delivery, logistics, and full-lifecycle sustainment of compiled AN/BYG-1 software baselines. This includes current, future, and legacy AN/BYG-1 applications as part of a modernized capability delivery framework. Key objectives and technical efforts under this contract include: Deliver AN/BYG-1 capabilities and baselines in alignment with Submarine Tactical Requirements Group priorities Decouple AN/BYG-1 applications from hardware and software dependencies Implement microcontainer/microservices AN/BYG-1 architecture Transform AN/BYG-1 development and test environments by increasing virtualization and establishing a common, shared infrastructure Develop and integrate tactical decision aids that leverage artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies Assist with the design, development, and integration of combat control system elements to support international cooperative agreements and joint programs. ACCESS TO SOLICITATION DOCUMENTS AND CLASSIFIED DATA The AN/BYG-1 Applications solicitation, Statement of Work (SOW), and associated unclassified attachments are designated as Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and will not be posted directly to SAM.gov. These documents will be made available exclusively via the secure Electronic Technical Information Center (E-TIC) portal hosted by the Advanced Interactive Management Technology Center (AIMTC). Additionally, portions of the Government Furnished Information, specifically, the classified software source code provided to support proposal development are classified at the SECRET level and will be transmitted physically. Documents made available during this procurement may contain classified data and/or technical data whose export is restricted by the Arms Export Control Act. Foreign participation shall be limited by applicable legal authorities, regulations, and other security classification requirements as specified in the DD Form 254. The IUID definition at DFARS 211.274-1 says IUID "is a system of marking, valuing and tracking items delivered to DoD." These spares are non-CLSSA FMS assets and will never be delivered to DoD. The assets are delivered to a domestic U.S. freight forwarder who is under contract by the FMS customer to ship the assets to the country of record. These parts will never be owned by the U.S. Government, and will never be entered into the DoD supply chain. The contractor shall submit repair procedures for Government approval prior to repair if those procedures deviate from the repair procedures detailed in the applicable repair specifications. REQUIREMENTS GENERAL REQUIREMENTS: The Contractor shall provide at the contractors facility the necessary repair labor, new and serviceable reworked repair parts, materials and test equipmentand arrange for outside services as required to return the equipment to a serviceable condition within the calendar day shop time as specified in the delivery schedule of the contract. SCOPE OF WORK FOR REPAIR: The scope of the work in the following subparagraphs are applicable to the latest configuration of the Government equipment.There shall be a 100% repair rate on all CLIN carcasses. Any carcass that cannot be repaired must have Defense Contract Mnagement Command (DCMC) Quality Assurance Representative(QAR) approval for disposal. Upon receipt of Government equipment the contractor shall perform incoming inspections, recording any shipping damage, and inventory components for completeness. Units with missing parts will not be inducted until missing partsare received or unless specifically authorized by the Procurment Contracting Officer (PCO). The contractor shall advise the PCO if any portion of the required servicing is a result of the furnishing by the contractor of articles that were defective in material and/or workmanship or otherwise not in conformance with the requirements of the contract under which such government equipment were originally furnished. In the event that the failed assembly is found to be beyond economical repair (BER), as defined in the contract, or in the event that the Government equipment is received with one or more subassemblies missing (FOR EXAMPLE: AS ARESULT OF CANNABALIZATION BY AN AIRCRAFT OPERATING SITE),the contractor shall promptly obtain confirmation of such findings from the cognizant DCMC QAR. and upon confirmation promptly notify the PCO for authority to scrap if BER and,if missing subassemblies, proceed IAW Missing on Induction (MOI).Units with missing parts will not be inducted until missing parts are received or unless specifically authorized by the PCO. All disassembly, repair and assembly of the Government equipment shall be IAW current engineering drawings and configuration specifications. All detail parts shall be inspected IAW the applicable repair specification and repaired or replaced as indicated. Replaced hardware shall be in accordance with the latest drawing revisions.The contractor shall provide and may use new or repaired/reworked parts which meet the requirements of the repair specification to restore the Government equipment in the delivery time specified in the contract. Repaired/reworked parts shall be used in lieu of new whenever possible as allowed by the applicable repair specification.Any repair of lower assemblies and/or detail parts not authorized by the by the applicable repair specification shall be submitted to the QAR for Government review and approval.Requests for repair approvals shall be accompanied by details of the repair and other applicable data such as tests which have been performed to validate the repair. Repaired Government equipment shall meet the inspection and acceptance test requirements of the applicable repair specifications. A contractor QA representative shall be required, in accordance with MIL-I-45208A, or ISO Quality standard equivalent, to witness repair,inspection, and acceptance tests Government representatives shall be notified of, and permitted to witnesssuch inspections at their discretion. The contractor shall submit repair procedures for Government approval prior to repair if those procedures deviate from the repair procedures detailed in the applicable repair specifications. Where the test specifications are found to be missing,inadequate,or behind in revision for a CLIN,the contractor shall develop and submit its own acceptance test procedures for Government approval to submission of the CLIN for Government acceptance. During the repair effort the contractor shall make no modifications to the CLIN that would prohibit future repair or require additional repair steps by other qualified sources. REPAIR PARTS: The contractor shall be responsible for identification, selection, ordering, and stocking of required piece parts to support all repairs. By definition," piece part" shall be any part or material listed in the applicable repair specification. TEST EQUIPMENT: The contractor will provide a laboratory facility equipped with instrumentation and testing capability for comprehensive functional testing of the equipment and detailed inspections of subassemblies and detailed parts. The contractor test equipment shall be designed to ensure repaired Government equipment function in full compliance with the requirementsof the applicable repair specification. All Government equipment's electrical performance and mechanical parameters shall be measured in accordance with the requirements of the applicable repair specification,with hard copy reports of all measurements available to the Government upon request. REQUIREMENTS The contractor shall maintain a quality control system which meets the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q 9858,ISO-9000 / 9001 / 9002 or equivalent. RESPONSIBILITY FOR INSPECTION: Unless otherwise specified, the contractor is responsible for the performance of all inspection requirements as specified herein. Except as otherwise specified, the contractor may use his own or any other facility suitable for the performance of the inspection requirements specified herein. PROCEDURES:The contractor shall prepare and maintain Quality Control Documentation, test and repair procedures, and inspection procedures which shall be made available to the Government for review and approval. The procedures shall include sequential diagrams of the test, repair, and inspection process, as well as the performance spcifications to perform the procedures. QUALITY ASSURANCE PROGRAM PLAN: The contractor shall develop, implement and maintain a Repair Quality Plan in compliance with the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q-9858, ISO,9000 / 9001 / 9002, or equvalent.The plan shall define the specific methods by which compliance with contractual requirements will be assured. All quality assurance data shall be provided to the Government for review and approval upon request. PURCHASED MATERIAL CONTROL: The contractor shall establish and maintain a system of control over purchased material which shall assure that the necessary requirements of this contract are included. in all sub contract agreements. A parts control system shall establish a record of performance for each purchased and internally manufactured part and shall be used to evaluate continued use of the source. The contractors control system shall be in compliance wil either Mil-I 45208A/Mil-Q-9858 or equivalent Quality Quality Assurance Standared.(ISO/AS:9000, 9001, 9002). RECEIVING INSPECTION OF PURCHASED MATERIAL: Purchased items shall be inspected upon receipt at the contractors facility to assure conformance with all requirements of the Technical Data Package (TDP). Evidence of such inspections shall be maintained for Government review at least twelve (12) months following acceptance of the end item. Inspection reports shall be maintained by the contractor. The inspection report shall, at a minimum, include a record of all dimensional data (coordinate/positional), material, finish, and process with appropriate pass/fail criteria, such ascertifications, and actual dimensional readings. FAILURE ANALYSIS AND CORRECTIVE ACTION:All failure analysis and corrective action reports/plans shall be submitted to the Government. NONCONFORMING MATERIAL:The contractor shall establish an effective system for controlling nonconforming material including procedures for identification, segregation, and disposition. CONTRACTOR INTERNAL REVIEW BOARD (IRB):IRB authority is delegated to the contractor for this contract only. The IRB may be used only for disposition of materials exhibiting minor non-conformances, scrap or rework to return a part to conformance with drawings or specifications as authorized by the approved repair procedures.IRB shall not use "AS-IS" disposition. A complete file of IRB actions shall be maintained for review by the Government for concurrance of classification. MATERIAL REVIEW BOARD (MRB):Formal MRB authority for disposition of "AS-IS"and for minor non-conformances is retained by the Government. The contractor shall submit the appropriate request for Variance via the DCMC to the NAVSUP Contracting Officer. RESPONSIBILITY FOR COMPLIANCE: All items must meet all requirements of this Statement of Work. The inspection requirements set forth in this SOW shall become part of the contractors overall inspection system or quality program. The absence of any inspection requirements in the SOW shall not relieve the contractor of the responsibility of assuring that all Government equipment submitted for acceptance comply with all requirements. Sampling in quality conformance does not authorize submission of known defective items, either indicated or actual, nor does it commit the procuring activity to acceptance of any defective items. REPAIR ASSESSMENT TESTING: The Government may select samples of the Contract Line Items (CLINS) which have completed repair and have been accepted by the Government representative for the purpose of conducting performance testing, environmental testing, and quality conformance examination in a repair assessment test program. A quantity of CLIN's may be randomly selected from each quaterly repair production completion for shipment to the CFA or other Government designated location to conduct this testing. RECORDS OF DATA COLLECTION: The contractor shall maintain a historical record file to contain copies of applicable data and documents for individual CLIN's and assemblies by CLIN serial number. The historical record file shall include,but not be limited to the following types of historical records: Receipt inspection documentation. Repair shop travelers or repair cards. REQUIREMENTS The contractor shall maintain a quality control system which meets the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q 9858,ISO-9000 / 9001 / 9002 or equivalent. RESPONSIBILITY FOR INSPECTION: Unless otherwise specified, the contractor is responsible for the performance of all inspection requirements as specified herein. Except as otherwise specified, the contractor may use his own or any other facility suitable for the performance of the inspection requirements specified herein. PROCEDURES:The contractor shall prepare and maintain Quality Control Documentation, test and repair procedures, and inspection procedures which shall be made available to the Government for review and approval. The procedures shall include sequential diagrams of the test, repair, and inspection process, as well as the performance spcifications to perform the procedures. QUALITY ASSURANCE PROGRAM PLAN: The contractor shall develop, implement and maintain a Repair Quality Plan in compliance with the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q-9858, ISO,9000 / 9001 / 9002, or equvalent.The plan shall define the specific methods by which compliance with contractual requirements will be assured. All quality assurance data shall be provided to the Government for review and approval upon request. PURCHASED MATERIAL CONTROL: The contractor shall establish and maintain a system of control over purchased material which shall assure that the necessary requirements of this contract are included. in all sub contract agreements. A parts control system shall establish a record of performance for each purchased and internally manufactured part and shall be used to evaluate continued use of the source. The contractors control system shall be in compliance wil either Mil-I 45208A/Mil-Q-9858 or equivalent Quality Quality Assurance Standared.(ISO/AS:9000, 9001, 9002). RECEIVING INSPECTION OF PURCHASED MATERIAL: Purchased items shall be inspected upon receipt at the contractors facility to assure conformance with all requirements of the Technical Data Package (TDP). Evidence of such inspections shall be maintained for Government review at least twelve (12) months following acceptance of the end item. Inspection reports shall be maintained by the contractor. The inspection report shall, at a minimum, include a record of all dimensional data (coordinate/positional), material, finish, and process with appropriate pass/fail criteria, such ascertifications, and actual dimensional readings. FAILURE ANALYSIS AND CORRECTIVE ACTION:All failure analysis and corrective action reports/plans shall be submitted to the Government. NONCONFORMING MATERIAL:The contractor shall establish an effective system for controlling nonconforming material including procedures for identification, segregation, and disposition. CONTRACTOR INTERNAL REVIEW BOARD (IRB):IRB authority is delegated to the contractor for this contract only. The IRB may be used only for disposition of materials exhibiting minor non-conformances, scrap or rework to return a part to conformance with drawings or specifications as authorized by the approved repair procedures.IRB shall not use "AS-IS" disposition. A complete file of IRB actions shall be maintained for review by the Government for concurrance of classification. title: A-E Environmental Program at Robins AFB, GA
description: SUBJECT: ARCHITECT-ENGINEER (A-E) ENVIRONMENTAL SERVICES ID/IQ: TITLE I, TITLE II, AND OTHER A-E SERVICES TO ADMINISTER, COORDINATE AND TECHNICALLY SUPPORT ENVIRONMENTAL PROGRAMS OF INTEREST TO THE GOVERNMENT Agency: Department of the Air Force Office: Air Force Materiel Command Location: WR-ALC POC: PCO Tad Williams CONTRACT INFORMATION Requirements Contract for Title I, Title II, and Other A-E Environmental Services. The basic award period will be for one year from the date of award. In addition, there will be four annual option years. The applicable NAICS is 541620, Size Standard: $19M. A-E Selection procedures will be used to competitively award one ID/IQ contracts using full and open competition. There will be only ONE contract awarded. This contract will be non-commercial with the use of Firm-Fixed Price (FFP), Time and Material (T&M), and Cost Reimbursement - No Fee (CRNF) contract line items (CLINs). The period of performance for the contract will be five years, a basic year plus four annual option years. The anticipated date of award is September 2026. REQUIRED SERVICES A detailed Statement of Work (SOW) for the subject Requirements contract is provided, along with an Appendix C, and Contract Data Requirements Lists (CDRLS). In general the required services under the subject Requirements contract will include: a) Title I Services Title I services include all aspects of design such as preparation and/or review of studies, plans, specifications, drawings, calculations, CAD, scheduling, cost estimates, regulatory and safety reviews, value engineering, and preparation of design and constructability reports, and operating and design manuals. They consist of conducting reviews of existing data, information, and reports, as well as conducting field surveys and investigations to obtain further data to prepare documentation as identified above. Title I efforts also encompass those efforts required to support and develop design work, including planning and programming, program management, project scoping, studies, investigations, evaluations, consultations, conceptual design, value engineering, facilities updates and modifications, topographic survey services, as well as operation, monitoring, and optimization of environmental treatment and/or control. b) Title II Construction Related Services The Contractor shall perform quality assurance and oversight of environmental projects, as well as other Title II A-E services. These activities can be related to specific or proposed projects, and can consist of construction related supervision and inspections, and constructability reviews. Supervision and inspection services are separate, normal construction management duties to include construction contractor submittal review, day to day liaison, surveillance, coordination, testing, and documentation of construction/investigative activities. Inspection activities ensure compliance with contract regulatory requirements, construction of complete and usable facilities, safe work practices, timely construction, limitation of cost growth, etc. All activities are under the jurisdiction of the CO and coordinated with MXDEU and/or Robins AFB Project Managers. Quality Assurance/Quality Control (QA/QC) inspection services will provide field work inspection being conducted by other contractors engaged in projects. This QA/QC inspection could include observation, data collection, validation, and conditions verification for any of the following: drilling and installation/development of monitoring wells, soil, ground water, and soil gas sampling, installation of extraction trenches, slurry walls, landfill caps, liners, and other construction and demolition activities; and production, process, and infrastructure investigations, disassembly, cleaning, refurbishment, replacement, modification, or demolition, Others as requested by the PCO. The Contractor will perform services similar to Title I but of a more detailed or final nature. These duties would include final design calculations, analyses, and/or drawings; definitive plans, final specifications; design support travel; design reviews, quality assurance, and oversight; cost estimates; procedure; and bid package development. c) Other A-E Services / Emergency & Imminent Danger Responses These efforts include planning and programming, program management, scoping, studies, operations support including data gathering and permit preparation, investigations including geophysical and process, evaluations, surveys, consultations, conceptual design, value engineering, as well as operation, monitoring, and optimization of environmental treatment or control systems, technical orders, updates or modifications, and documentation. Also included are other related services for the continuation of these existing programs or to establish initial ones. As part of Other A-E Services it is noted that Emergency and Imminent Danger responses are included. Robins Air Force Base, and its satellite areas, conducts a wide variety of industrial and commercial processes involving a broad range of equipment, materials, liquids, and solids. The Contractor shall provide a full range of services to satisfactorily address these situations. description: What are the hours of operation for Generator Maintenance? This is in the SOW Can you provide a Document with each Back-up Generator Model # s &Serial # s? This is Attachment A of the package Please Confirm the Voltage of the Generators? 480 and 240 Regarding Contractor Provided Consumables, many of the items listed are typically repairs quoted and approved before work proceeds on this and some parts(hoses and belts). As an outside vendor there is no way to effectively build this into your maintenance plan to guarantee effective cost for both the vendor and for Edward Hines VA. We request this section is altered to allow for these costs to be sectioned out for repairs and for one annual service to replace filters and oil.� See Attachment B. How many Generators have Diesel Engines?� All of them Are there any Generators with difficulty accessing (Roof, Parking Garage, Basement)? If so, which units are they? NO Are your Generators within 50 ft of the Entry Door, where our truck will be parked? Yes Are the Annual Load Tests performed with your Minor B-PMs? No Can I get the age of each equipment if possible? See Attachment A Please clarify the Unscheduled Repair CLIN amount. Is the stated $50,000 intended to mean $50,000 per contract year? This is just a funding item for me to populate an unscheduled maintenance clin for me to address items the break. Where should emergency travel and labor be priced? All previous contracts has local labor. Never had this issue. Build it in your quote. Will VA furnish diesel consumed during inspections? VA furnishes Fuel for the generators Period. Can you provide any previous maintenance reports, emergency calls, major repairs, etc.? After Award. Consumables Attachment Section 2.1 states Replace PM Consumables as required and references Attachment 1, while the solicitation package includes Generator Consumables Attachment B. Please confirm that Attachment B is the document intended by the reference to Attachment 1, and that the consumables identified in Attachment B are to be furnished and replaced by the contractor as required during preventive maintenance and included within the applicable PM CLIN pricing. Consumables are outlined in Attachment B. Work Hours / Load Bank Testing Section 4.3 identifies the monthly PM for the two 600 kW generators and one 500 kW generator as occurring on the second Tuesday of each month from 4:00 AM to 7:00 AM, while the 1250 kW and 750 kW generators may be serviced during normal business hours. Please confirm whether the annual load-bank testing, ATS maintenance, sampling, and other annual maintenance activities may also be performed during normal business hours unless otherwise coordinated with the COR. The 600 s, and 500 are backing up a critical production line that is old and has issues during power transfers. We require them and their associated equipment to be cycled or maintained prior to that department s workday start, so they can start the production line on time with no delay. This department is the Consolidated Mail Order Pharmacy (CMOP). All the generator maintenance is to be performed on the second Tuesday of each month, we need the CMOP Generators started and done first. Transformer Annual Inspection and IR Scan The scope includes quarterly energized transformer inspections as well as an annual inspection that includes additional maintenance activities and an IR scan. The pricing schedule only provides a quarterly transformer CLIN with a quantity of four. Please confirm whether the annual transformer inspection and IR scan are to be included within the pricing for the four quarterly inspections, with one quarterly service incorporating the annual work, or if the annual service is to be priced separately. Please confirm the intended operating condition for the annual IR scan, as it appears under the annual de-energized inspection section. Annual Transformer and ATS IR Scanning Procedure The annual infrared (IR) scan of transformer lugs and automatic transfer switches (ATSs) is to be completed while the equipment is energized, prior to any deenergizing procedures. This approach allows for the identification of potential faults under operating conditions, ensuring that any issues are detected before maintenance begins. Once the IR scan is performed, any necessary repairs should be made during the scheduled deenergized maintenance period. This ensures that faults identified during the scan can be addressed safely while the equipment is not under load. The IR scan should occur once each year and, whenever possible, should be scheduled close to the time of the annual deenergized maintenance. This coordination facilitates efficient fault resolution and minimizes downtime. In the event of an emergent issue identified during the scan, immediate corrective action will be taken to address the problem as soon as possible, regardless of the scheduled maintenance cycle.

title: Industry Day - Sentinel Utility Infrastructure Improvements at MAFB
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Seattle District, intends to conduct a virtual Industry Day to provide industry partners with information regarding the Sentinel Utility Infrastructure Improvements project including the intended acquisition approach utilizing Other Transaction Authority via Construction Management at Risk. The purpose will be to gather feedback and foster open communication between government and industry. Event Details: Date: 21 October 2026 Time: 0900-1200 PT Format: Virtual (Link will be provided to registered attendees 1 day prior to the event) Registration Due Date: 19 October 2026 Who Should Attend: All interested vendors, including small businesses, large businesses, and other industry partners. Attendance at this event is not mandatory. Event link will be provided to those that complete the event registration via the link provided below. PROJECT BACKGROUND The Sentinel (Ground Based Strategic Deterrent) program is modernizing the Nation�s land-based intercontinental ballistic missile force. At Malmstrom AFB, the Air Force is constructing a suite of new facilities collectively referred to as the Operations and Maintenance Complex (OMC), together with associated support facilities. The Utility Infrastructure Project is the critical enabling backbone that must be in place before the remaining Sentinel facilities can be constructed and made operational. Scope of the Utility Infrastructure Improvements project includes construction of a comprehensive utilities distribution system serving the entire Sentinel GBSD Complex at Malmstrom AFB. Primary elements include: Electrical distribution systems, including connection to / expansion of electrical substation capacity as required to serve the new campus. Water distribution and related appurtenances. Wastewater collection and connection to treatment systems. Natural gas service to the campus. Telecommunications backbone connectivity, including fiber services to Information Transfer Nodes (ITNs), electrical substation, water pump stations, and related Base utility facilities. Associated site work: clearing, grubbing, grading, minor demolition, drainage, utility and communications connections, access paving, parking, and walkways as applicable. title: AC/MC-130J Arkham SMP Production
description: Arkham Special Mission Processor (SMP): The Government is conducting market research to identify potential sources that possess the expertise, capabilities, facilities, and experience to manufacture, assemble, test, and deliver a total of 94 Arkham SMP Production Kits and 55 Spares. The Arkham SMP is a mission processor utilizing Sensor Open System Architecture (SOSA) in support of AC/MC-130J system integration. The Arkham SMP is separated into two (2) major processing areas: Video Processing/General Processing and Safety Critical Processing. The Video Processing/General Processing is done on five (5) Intel based General Purpose Processor Modules. The Safety Critical Processing is done on two (2) ARM based Safety Critical Processor (SCP) modules. The network includes a red and an internal NextGen SMP gold (same classified level with different subnets), and two unclassified black for multiple levels of security. Safety Critical Processing is separated into Red/Gold and Black zones. The Arkham SMP must utilize LYNXOS and Red Hat Enterprise Linux as the operating system. The acquisition strategy is for the contractor to provide kit production with a period of performance of seven (7) Years. The kit will include the following: Two (2) Arkham Units, two (2) External Data Storage (EDS) Devices, two (2) one (1) TB Delkin Solid State Drives (SSD), and other hardware required for aircraft installation. This will provide the AC/MC-130J mission with enhanced abilities for search and rescue in increased threat environments. Potential Sources must be capable of developing prototype hardware, software, and all associated technical data necessary to be able to produce and deliver the Arkham Production Kit and Spares. The Potential Source must be able to fully test and evaluate the function and performance of the Arkham Production Kit and Spares. The Potential Source must be capable of developing and providing the source data necessary to update AFTO�s and TDPs.

Requirements Description: The load bank is a piece of electrical test equipment used to simulate an electrical load, to test an electric power source. The load bank is used to provide field preventive maintenance checks and services of the Electric Power Plant (EPP III) on the PATRIOT Missile Defense System. The EPP III is the main electric power source for the PATRIOT Missile Defense System. The load banks are used on the 15 KW,30KW, and 150 KW, 400Hz generator sets on the EPP III. The load banks must meet the requirements of the CECOM Purchase Description (PD) #A3357168 Rev A and A3354293 Rev A. The PD can be obtained by writing via email to david.teicher.civ@army.mil.We are looking for brand name or equal load banks meeting the requirements of the PD, at a minimum, which will also include load cables. title: Improved Data Collection, Monitoring and Revenue Base for Water Resource Management in Kenya
description: This Assignment is financed from official Danish development assistance through the Danish Africa Water facility (Danish Finance Act § 06.32.01.32). Emphasis is therefore on providing safe and affordable access to water for all (Sustainable Development Goal 6.1), increase water-use efficiency and ensure freshwater supplies (Sustainable Development Goal 6.4) and to raise capacity for planning and management of climate change (Sustainable Goal 13.5). The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Royal Danish Embassy, Nairobi (RDE) is the funding agency and Water Resources Authority (WRA) is the Recipient of the outcome of the Assignment. The Assignment aims at operating with a high level of local content by engaging local partners with the view of increasing the long-term sustainability of digital systems and ease of their future maintenance as well as enhanced dialogue on water use with local communities. The Water Resources Authority (WRA) is a state corporation established under Section 11 of the Water Act, 2016 and mandated to regulate the management and use of Kenya's water resources on behalf of the national government. WRA formulates standards and regulations, issues and enforces water permits, sets water-use fees, and advises the Cabinet Secretary on national water-resource policy. WRA operates through a decentralised structure comprising one head office, six basin offices, 26 sub-basins, eight laboratories and three satellite offices. WRA is currently undertaking the development of an Enterprise Architecture as part of the Government’s Digitization of Government Services Performance Contracting initiative, in alignment with the Government Enterprise Architecture framework and applicable Government ICT standards. Kenya has a comparatively clear formal water-resource governance architecture, but implementation is constrained by incomplete coordination across national, basin, county and sub-catchment levels, limited basin and sub-basin resources, and overlapping institutional interfaces. WRA already operates digital permitting, e-billing, smart-metering, hydrological monitoring, GIS and laboratory systems; however, these features remains fragmented and have not yet been demonstrated to provide an end-to-end authoritative record linking the water user and abstraction point to the permit, meter, reading, invoice, payment, inspection and hydrological context. The core information-management challenge is not the absence of digital systems, but their fragmentation across field monitoring, permitting, metering, billing, enforcement and hydrological decision support. WRA is working to create integrations between its various IT solutions, but the vision for this project is to support components in establishing a single point of entry/IT solution—hereinafter referred to as WRIMS—that will ensure integration among all existing IT solutions, as shown in the diagram below and elaborated in the background document on WRA’s existing IT environment. The Assignment regarding Improved Data Collection, Monitoring and Revenue Base for Water Resource Management in Kenya (hereafter “IMPRODATWRM”) is expected to be designed to close the institutional and information-management gap while strengthening WRA's own-source revenue base and the evidence available for sustainable allocation. The Assignment is to support WRA in transforming its fragmented digital landscape into an integrated, interoperable WRIMS environment that connects the full operating chain - from registration and permitting through meter/device management, reliable measurement, validation, billing, payment reconciliation, inspection and enforcement, and will connect these regulatory transactions to basin-level hydrological information. Shared identifiers, GIS references, data-governance rules and interoperable interfaces are essential across this chain. The Assignment is to support WRA in transforming its fragmented digital landscape into an integrated, interoperable WRIMS environment that connects the full operating chain - from registration and permitting through meter/device management, reliable measurement, validation, billing, payment reconciliation, inspection and enforcement, and will connect these regulatory transactions to basin-level hydrological information. Shared identifiers, GIS references, data-governance rules and interoperable interfaces are essential across this chain. The Assignment will align with and leverage the resulting business, data, application, technology and security architectures to guide the design and implementation of WRIMS, while supporting the operationalisation of the EA, particularly in systems integration, interoperability, data governance, ICT infrastructure and cybersecurity. The Assignment is divided into three phases: Phase I: Detailed verification, system analysis and preparation Phase II: A Kenyan-led option assessment and decision Phase III: Design, build, test, roll-out and stabilised operation

title: Germany – Metalworking – Metallbau- , Schlosserarbeiten
description: Auf dem Gelände der Marineunteroffizierschule in Plön ist der Bau von zwei neuen Unterkunftsgebäuden geplant, Gebäude 47 und Gebäude 54. Diese werden auf zwei separaten, nicht miteinander verbundenen Baufeldern auf der Liegenschaft erstellt. Die Erschließung erfolgt über das Haupttor der Kaserne. Die Flächen sind verkehrstechnisch über die befestigten Straßenflächen innerhalb des Geländes erschlossen. Der Neubau des Unterkunftsgebäudes 47 soll auf einer ehemaligen Waldfläche an der südöstlichen Grenze des Geländes realisiert werden. Das Grundstück wird im Rahmen des Bauvorhabens an die bestehende Infrastruktur der Liegenschaft angeschlossen. Das Baufeld umfasst ca. 5.860m². Der Neubau des Unterkunftsgebäudes 54 ist auf der Fläche zwischen den Gebäuden 53 und der RÜH (Rettungsübungshalle) geplant. Das Grundstück ist an die bestehende Infrastruktur der Liegenschaft angeschlossen. Das Baufeld umfasst ca. 2.400m². Die viergeschossigen Gebäude mit einer Gesamtabmessung von 57,70 m x 14,16 m sind mit einem 43° geneigten Satteldach versehen und werden über zwei Treppenräume an der Längsseite erschlossen. Die Traufhöhe beträgt 10,50 m, die Firsthöhe beträgt 17,10 m. Es handelt sich um Massivbauten mit Mauerwerkswänden, Stahlbetondecken und einem Dachstuhl in Holzbauweise. In jedem Neubau sind jeweils 81 Einzelunterkünfte untergebracht. Für die Dauer des BVH im Zeitraum ca. III. Q 2026 bis ca. IV. title: Zambia – Water pumps – Bau von Solar-PV-Stromerzeugungssystemen und Austausch und Sanierung von Pumpensystemen
description: Das Projekt „Nexus Energy Water Programme for Zambia“ (NEWZA) zielt darauf ab, die Verflechtung zwischen dem Energie- und dem Wassersektor zu stärken. Das Projekt wird von der Europäischen Union (EU) und dem Bundesministerium für wirtschaftliche Zusammenarbeit und Entwicklung (BMZ) der Bundesrepublik Deutschland über die KfW kofinanziert. Das NEWZA-Programm umfasst auch laufende Projekte, die von der deutschen Bundesregierung kofinanziert werden, nämlich: • Programm „Städtische Wasserversorgung und Abwasserentsorgung in der Ostprovinz, Phase IV“ (BMZ-Nr.: 2016 67 328/2018 67 514/2018 70 104) und • Management von Wasserressourcen und Abwasserentsorgung für mittelgroße Städte (BMZ-Nr.: 2020 67 494, 2022 70 023). Das Ziel von NEWZA ist es, den Zugang zu grüner Energie und Wasserversorgung für alle zu verbessern, indem die Leistungsfähigkeit von fünf sambischen Wasserversorgungsunternehmen gesteigert wird: Southern (Los 1), Chambeshi (Los 2), Lukanga (Los 3), Nkana (Los 4) und Eastern (Los 5). Die Arbeiten werden auf der Grundlage des FIDIC-Vertrags für Anlagen und Design-Build-Verträge, 1. Auflage 1999 (Yellow Book), vergeben. Der Arbeitsumfang für alle kommerziellen Versorgungsunternehmen ist nachstehend aufgeführt. Diese Liste dient lediglich der Veranschaulichung des Umfangs und ist nicht als vollständige Auflistung zu verstehen. Der Arbeitsumfang umfasst: ► Komponente 1 Solar-PV • Projektmanagement, Planung, Installation und Inbetriebnahme der Solaranlagen liegen in der Verantwortung des Auftragnehmers • Das Grundstück für die PV-Anlagen wird entweder innerhalb der Produktions-/Entnahme-/Aufbereitungsanlagen und/oder anderen Standorten der CU bereitgestellt. Reicht die Fläche nicht aus, wird das Grundstück von der CU durch Kauf oder Pacht gesichert • Installation von Online-Überwachungsplattformen für PV-Anlagen, einschließlich Echtzeit-Datenerfassung, -übertragung (GPRS/GSM oder andere), sicherer Cloud-Datenspeicherung und Online-Portalschnittstelle (sicherheitsgeschützt) mit Anzeige der Infrastrukturzustands-/Leistungsdaten auf Standortebene • Betrieb und Wartung für bis zu 2 Jahre nach der Planungs- und Bauphase Teilkomponente 1a – Netzgekoppelte Solar-PV-Anlagen • Entwurf und Lieferung von netzgekoppelten Solarstromanlagen für die bestehenden Wassergewinnungs-/Wasserentnahme-/Wasseraufbereitungsanlagen und/oder andere Standorte der CU. Die Größe der PV-Anlagen ist durch die Kapazität der vorhandenen Nieder-/Mittelspannungs- und Transformatoranlagen begrenzt. • Dies umfasst die Installation von Solar-PV-Modulen, Anschlusskästen, Verkabelung, Filtern (falls erforderlich), Wechselrichtern, Sammelschienenverlängerungen und Niederspannungsfächern (falls erforderlich). • Durchführung von Standortmessungen der Stromdaten zum Vergleich des Stromverbrauchs vor und nach den Arbeiten. Bei Standorten, an denen Pumpen saniert werden, Bewertung des Anteils des Jahresverbrauchs nach der Pumpensanierung. Teilkomponente 1b – Hybride Solar-PV-Anlagen • Entwurf und Lieferung von hybriden Solar-PV-Anlagen für die bestehenden Wassergewinnungs-/Wasserentnahme-/Wasseraufbereitungsanlagen und/oder andere Standorte der CU. Die Größe der Anlage richtet sich nach der Pumpeneingangsleistung (P1) und der Anzahl der Arbeitspumpen. • An Standorten, an denen Hybridtechnologie zum Einsatz kommt, werden auch die Pumpen und die zugehörigen Stromversorgungsanlagen ausgetauscht. • Dies umfasst die Installation von Solar-PV-Modulen, Anschlusskästen, Filtern (nach Bedarf), Hybrid-Wechselrichtern, Niederspannungsausrüstung für Solar-PV und Pumpen sowie Frequenzumrichtern für Pumpen. Der Umfang der Komponente umfasst die Schnittstelle oder Grenze am Anschlusspunkt für die Kabel von der Niederspannungsausrüstung zu den Pumpen. • Online-Überwachungsplattformen für Standorte, an denen das Hybridsystem in ein einziges System für Pumpen und Solar-PV integriert ist. ► Komponente 2 – Pumpensysteme • Sanierung der bestehenden Pumpensystembeklebung, im Wesentlichen: Pumpen, Kabel, Niederspannungs- und Mittelspannungsschalttafeln, Ventile/Armaturen, Rohrleitungen der Pumpstation, Mess- und Regelgeräte • Projektmanagement, Planung, Installation und Inbetriebnahme der Pumpensysteme in Verantwortung des Auftragnehmers • Das System ist auf gleichbleibende oder erhöhte zukünftige Tagesdurchflussmengen gemäß den Anforderungen der CU ausgelegt. Die täglichen Durchflussmengen und die vorgesehenen Betriebsstunden werden in der Ausschreibung angegeben. • Überprüfung des Betriebsdrucks der Steigleitung durch Tests vor Ort, Ermittlung hydraulischer Probleme (nicht funktionierende Luftventile) und Messung der tatsächlichen Durchflussmengen vor Ort und des Energieverbrauchs der Pumpen (alle Betriebsmodi). Die geschätzten Nennleistungen der Pumpen (Durchfluss, Druck, Nennmotorleistung) werden in der Ausschreibung nur zu Informationszwecken angegeben. Die endgültige Dimensionierung der Pumpen zur Erfüllung der Durchflussanforderungen liegt in der Verantwortung des Auftragnehmers. • Installation eines digitalen Online-Fernüberwachungssystems, das an wichtige Messgeräte (Durchfluss, Druck und Leistung) angeschlossen ist, mit einem 3-Jahres-Abonnement (falls zutreffend) für den Zugang. Keine Fernsteuerung der Systeme. • Technischer Support, Betrieb und Wartung für bis zu 2 Jahre Das Projekt muss in Übereinstimmung mit den KfW-Nachhaltigkeitsrichtlinien vorbereitet und durchgeführt werden: https://www.kfw-entwicklungsbank.de/PDF/Download-Center/PDF-Dokumente-Richtlinien/Nachhaltigkeitsrichtlinie_EN.pdf

title: Denmark – Foreign economic-aid-related services – Improved Data Collection, Monitoring and Revenue Base for Water Resource Management in Kenya
description: This Assignment is financed from official Danish development assistance through the Danish Africa Water facility (Danish Finance Act § 06.32.01.32). Emphasis is therefore on providing safe and affordable access to water for all (Sustainable Development Goal 6.1), increase water-use efficiency and ensure freshwater supplies (Sustainable Development Goal 6.4) and to raise capacity for planning and management of climate change (Sustainable Goal 13.5). The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Royal Danish Embassy, Nairobi (RDE) is the funding agency and Water Resources Authority (WRA) is the Recipient of the outcome of the Assignment. The Assignment aims at operating with a high level of local content by engaging local partners with the view of increasing the long-term sustainability of digital systems and ease of their future maintenance as well as enhanced dialogue on water use with local communities. The Water Resources Authority (WRA) is a state corporation established under Section 11 of the Water Act, 2016 and mandated to regulate the management and use of Kenya's water resources on behalf of the national government. WRA formulates standards and regulations, issues and enforces water permits, sets water-use fees, and advises the Cabinet Secretary on national water-resource policy. WRA operates through a decentralised structure comprising one head office, six basin offices, 26 sub-basins, eight laboratories and three satellite offices. WRA is currently undertaking the development of an Enterprise Architecture as part of the Government’s Digitization of Government Services Performance Contracting initiative, in alignment with the Government Enterprise Architecture framework and applicable Government ICT standards. Kenya has a comparatively clear formal water-resource governance architecture, but implementation is constrained by incomplete coordination across national, basin, county and sub-catchment levels, limited basin and sub-basin resources, and overlapping institutional interfaces. WRA already operates digital permitting, e-billing, smart-metering, hydrological monitoring, GIS and laboratory systems; however, these features remains fragmented and have not yet been demonstrated to provide an end-to-end authoritative record linking the water user and abstraction point to the permit, meter, reading, invoice, payment, inspection and hydrological context. The core information-management challenge is not the absence of digital systems, but their fragmentation across field monitoring, permitting, metering, billing, enforcement and hydrological decision support. WRA is working to create integrations between its various IT solutions, but the vision for this project is to support components in establishing a single point of entry/IT solution—hereinafter referred to as WRIMS—that will ensure integration among all existing IT solutions, as shown in the diagram below and elaborated in the background document on WRA’s existing IT environment. The Assignment regarding Improved Data Collection, Monitoring and Revenue Base for Water Resource Management in Kenya (hereafter “IMPRODATWRM”) is expected to be designed to close the institutional and information-management gap while strengthening WRA's own-source revenue base and the evidence available for sustainable allocation. The Assignment is to support WRA in transforming its fragmented digital landscape into an integrated, interoperable WRIMS environment that connects the full operating chain - from registration and permitting through meter/device management, reliable measurement, validation, billing, payment reconciliation, inspection and enforcement, and will connect these regulatory transactions to basin-level hydrological information. Shared identifiers, GIS references, data-governance rules and interoperable interfaces are essential across this chain. Shared identifiers, GIS references, data-governance rules and interoperable interfaces are essential across this chain. The Assignment will align with and leverage the resulting business, data, application, technology and security architectures to guide the design and implementation of WRIMS, while supporting the operationalisation of the EA, particularly in systems integration, interoperability, data governance, ICT infrastructure and cybersecurity. The Assignment is divided into three phases: Phase I: Detailed verification, system analysis and preparation Phase II: A Kenyan-led option assessment and decision Phase III: Design, build, test, roll-out and stabilised operation

description: Die hochrangige Regierungsberatung wird in Staaten in Osteuropa, auf dem Westbalkan, im Südkaukasus und in Zentralasien durchgeführt. Aktuell erfolgt die Beratung in den Ländern Ukraine, Belarus (derzeit ausgesetzt), Moldau, Georgien (derzeit ausgesetzt), Usbekistan und Kosovo. Ab 2027 soll die Beratung in den Ländern Ukraine, Moldau, Usbekistan, Kosovo, Albanien und Nordmazedonien erfolgen. title: Denmark – Prefabricated buildings – Udbud af kontorpavilloner DTU Risø og DTU Lyngby
description: Udbud af pavilloner til Danmark Tekniske Universitets (fremover ”DTU”) lokationer i Risø og Lyngby. Udbuddet gennemføres som offentligt udbud efter udbudslovens §§ 56-57. Opgaven udbydes som en samlet totalentreprise, fordi DTU har vurderet, at projektets størrelse og ønsket om at pavillonerne kan flyttes og kombineres på tværs af lokation kræver, at opgaven ikke løses i flere selvstændige aftaler. De udbudte pavilloner er tiltænkt som flytbare enheder, således de løbende efter behov kan flyttes mellem lokationerne samt indbyrdes integreres og sammenbygges, når DTU's behov herfor opstår. Endvidere har DTU lagt vægt på, at DTU fungerer som én samlet bygherre på tværs af de omfattede lokationer, samt at der vurderes at kunne opnås økonomiske stordriftsfordele ved indkøb af et større samlet antal pavilloner hos én leverandør.

title: Denmark – Electrical machinery, apparatus, equipment and consumables; lighting – EU-udbud vedr. levering, installation og drift af ladepunkter til egen flåde i Sønderborg Kommune
description: Sønderborg Kommune, herefter benævnt ”Bygherre”, er i gang med en løbende udskiftning af den nuværende fossildrevne personbilflåde til elbiler. Bygherre ønsker derfor at etablere en række ladepunkter dedikeret til disse køretøjer på forskellige lokationer i kommunen. Selve indkøbet af elbiler er ikke en del af nærværende udbud. Nærværende udbud vedrører levering, installation og idriftsættelse af ladepunkter til en del af Sønderborg Kommunes kommunale køretøjer. Derudover vedrører udbuddet alle nødvendige elarbejder mellem tilslutningspunktet og ladepunkterne, samt planlægning, projektering og udførelse af alle grave- og reetableringsarbejder, som er nødvendige for at etablere infrastrukturen. Slutteligt vedrører udbuddet også service og vedligeholdelse af ladepunkterne samt levering af en softwareløsning i en 5-årig periode med mulighed for forlængelse af to (2) gange ét (1) år. Det er for Bygherre vigtigt at indgå et samarbejde med en Operatør, som har forståelse for, at ladepunkterne er kritisk infrastruktur, da dele af den kommunale flåde er hjemmeplejebiler, som benyttes i en samfundsmæssig vigtig opgave. Sønderborg Kommune skal eje de indkøbte ladebokse og ladestandere mv. Derudover betaler Sønderborg Kommune tilslutningsafgifter og det løbende strømforbrug afregnes direkte med elselskabet. Kontrakten vedrører følgende 4 lokationer i Fase 1 (i alt 196 ladepunkter): • Omsorg og Udvikling – Hjemmeplejen Distrikt Nordals, Nørreled 31, 6430 Nordborg • Omsorg og Udvikling – Hjemmeplejen Distrikt Fjord, Skovgade 13, 6320 Egernsund • Omsorg og Udvikling – Hjemmeplejen Distrikt Sydals, Tandsbjerg 10B, 6400 Sønderborg • Omsorg og Udvikling – Hjemmeplejen Distrikt Alssund, Kongevej 19, 6400 Sønderborg Derudover er der følgende optioner: • Option 1 vedrører 2 lokationer (i alt 32 ladepunkter) • Option 2 vedrører 5 lokationer (i alt 26 ladepunkter) • Option 3 vedrører 2 lokationer (i alt 20 ladepunkter) • Option A vedrører 38 eksisterende ladepunkter, fordelt på en række lokationer, af mærket ABB, som Bygherre ønsker overgår til et samlet driftssystem, hvis muligt • Option B vedrører 56 eksisterende ladepunkter, fordelt på en række lokationer, af mærket KEBA, som Bygherre ønsker overgår til et samlet driftssystem, hvis muligt I udbudsmaterialet anvendes både betegnelserne ”Operatøren” og ”Entreprenør”. Disse betegnelser er synonymer i nærværende materiale, og betegner den vindende tilbudsgiver, samt dennes underentreprenører, der indgås kontrakt med. Der henvises i øvrigt til definitionsliste i Kravspecifikationen. Det udbudte arbejde er mere detaljeret beskrevet i udbudsmaterialet.

title: Germany – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Integrierte energetische Quartierskonzepte, Sanierungsmanagements und strategische Gesamtprojektleitung für Huckarde / Westerfilde & Bodelschwingh
description: Die Stadt Dortmund verfolgt das Ziel, die Energiewende und die Transformation des Gebäudebestands auf Quartiersebene aktiv zu unterstützen. Die Ergebnisse der Kommunalen Wärmeplanung zeigen, dass insbesondere im privaten Gebäudebestand erhebliche Potenziale zur Reduzierung des Energieverbrauchs, zur Minderung von Treibhausgasemissionen und zur Umstellung auf erneuerbare Energieträger bestehen. Einzeleigentümer*innen, Wohnungsunternehmen, Gewerbetreibende sowie weitere lokale Akteur*innen stehen dabei vor komplexen technischen, wirtschaftlichen und organisatorischen Herausforderungen. Die Umsetzung entsprechender Maßnahmen erfordert insbesondere die Aktivierung und Begleitung dieser unterschiedlichen Zielgruppen. Es besteht ein hoher Bedarf an Information, Beratung, Vernetzung und Unterstützung bei der Entwicklung konkreter Vorhaben. Vor diesem Hintergrund beabsichtigt die Stadt Dortmund, für die Klimaquartiere Westerfilde & Bodelschwingh sowie Huckarde jeweils integrierte energetische Quartierskonzepte erarbeiten bzw. fortschreiben zu lassen und die Konzepterstellung begleitende und darauf aufbauende Sanierungsmanagements einzusetzen. Die Sanierungsmanagements sollen als Schnittstelle zwischen Verwaltung, Bürgerschaft, Eigentümer*innen, Wohnungswirtschaft, Energieversorgern und weiteren Akteur*innen wirken und die Umsetzung energetischer Sanierungs- und Transformationsprozesse im Quartier unterstützen. Der Auftrag umfasst sowohl strategische als auch operative Leistungen für beide Klimaquartiere. Die quartiersbezogenen Leistungen sollen durch eine strategische Gesamtprojektleitung koordiniert werden, die ebenfalls Gegenstand dieser Ausschreibung ist. Dabei sind gemeinsame Synergien und Transferpotenziale zwischen den Quartieren ebenso zu berücksichtigen wie quartiersspezifische Ausgangslagen und Anforderungen.
